leads.posting: Social gaming startup Matiks raises $10 Mn in Pre-Series A led by General Catalyst. Bengaluru-based social gaming startup Matiks has raised $10 million in a Pre-Series A funding round led by General Catalyst, with participation from Ronnie Screwvala and existing investors Info Edge Ventures, Tanglin Venture Partners and Untitled Ventures. The fresh capital will be used to expand its international presence, develop new games and social experiences, and launch an AI-powered game creation platform that will allow users to build and publish games without coding. Founded in 2024 by Sudhanshu Bhatia, Sushant and Mohan, Matiks started as a mental maths game and has since expanded into a social gaming platform offering games across mathematics, memory, logic and puzzles. The platform allows users to compete against friends, participate in daily challenges and track their progress. In September 2026, 2.2 million users played 48 million games on the platform. Its daily active users have more than doubled since June to over 300,000, with the company also seeing early traction in markets such as Japan, the US and South Korea. The company recently launched SNAC, an endless feed of single-player puzzles, which has contributed to longer user sessions, according to Matiks. Matiks plans to initially focus on the US market before expanding into other major international markets. It will also invest in engineering, artificial intelligence, product development, game design and growth. The company is also developing an AI-powered game creation engine that will enable users to create, publish and share their own brain games across multiple formats. In August 2025, Matiks raised $3.1 million in a Pre-Series A round led by Tanglin Venture Partners, with participation from Info Edge Ventures and angel investors, including boAt co-founder Aman Gupta and Unacademy co-founders Gaurav Munjal and Roman Saini, among others.

leads.posting: Luxury watch brand Rotoris raises Rs 70 Cr in Series A round led by Blume Ventures. Luxury watch brand Rotoris has raised Rs 70 crore (about $7.4 million) in a Series A funding round led by Blume Ventures. The round also saw participation from 9Unicorns, Centricity and a group of family offices, including Diwakar Goel, Atul Singh and Adhiraj Burman. Actor and television host Rannvijay Singha also participated in the round. The company will use the fresh capital for research and development, production expansion and the growth of its physical presence in India and overseas. Founded by Prerna Gupta and Aakash Anand, Rotoris operates an invitation only model through its Registry. The company said its first collection of 2,100 numbered watches sold out within days of its launch in February 2026. Nearly 100,000 people have since registered for access to its watches, with 40% of demand coming from markets outside India, including the US, Dubai and Australia. In December 2025, Rotoris raised $3 million in a seed funding round led by Zerodha co-founder Nikhil Kamath, actor-investor Vivek Anand Oberoi, Venture Catalysts, 100 Unicorns and Tanmay Bhat. The round also saw participation from more than 30 founders, including Mamaearth's Varun Alagh, Noise's Gaurav Khatri and Snitch's Siddharth Dungarwal. Rotoris offers collections such as Manifesta, which features natural stone dials, and Astonia, a chronograph built around a Swiss movement. Its watches are assembled and tested at the Rotoris Atelier in Gurugram, with movements sourced from Switzerland and Japan. The company plans to expand its physical presence through Rotoris House, with plans to move beyond Delhi to Mumbai and New York. Aakash Anand previously built and scaled beauty and personal care brand Bella Vita before exiting the business. Prerna Gupta leads Rotoris, with a focus on premium brand building and customer experience.

leads.posting: Fireside Ventures leads Rs 100 Cr Series B round in snack brand Troovy. Snack brand Troovy has raised Rs 100 crore in a Series B funding round led by Fireside Ventures, with participation from Sharrp Ventures and other investors. Entrackr had exclusively reported the fundraise in June this year, when the company was looking to raise up to Rs 200 crore in a Series B round. The Gurugram-based brand had previously raised $5 million in a Series A round in January this year. The round was led by Fireside Ventures and Sharrp Ventures, with participation from existing investors Spring Marketing Capital and Veltis Capital. Before that, the startup had raised $2.3 million (Rs 20 crore) in a pre-Series A round led by Fireside Ventures in May 2025. The proceeds will be used to expand R&D and manufacturing capacity, scale distribution across quick commerce and offline channels, and accelerate its Build Together model, Troovy said in a press release. Co-founded in 2023 by Aditya Mukherjee and Mansi Baranwal, Troovy is a food and snacking brand that offers products such as snacks, sauces, spreads and millet pasta. The brand focuses on using carefully selected ingredients to offer convenient food options for children and families. The company develops products based on parental inputs and insights into children's preferences. It aims to make better food choices more appealing through product innovation and a consumer-first approach. Troovy said its vacuum-cooked potato chips contain 10% to 12% oil, compared with 35% to 40% in mainstream chips. The company also offers clean-label ketchup and seasonings for children without synthetic additives or preservatives. The brand competes with Slurrp Farm, Timios and The Mumum Co in the kids' health food segment.
